budget_items.what_was_said: Town meeting passed the citizens' petition override by a very narrow margin; the board debated whether to call a special election.
A member noted last year's override already raised tax bills and a new one would add further, which is hard on seniors.

budget_items.topic: Free cash to offset not doing override

A member reported the state ways and means budget raised the minimum per-pupil aid increase, which could help the district's numbers.
Board members discussed preliminary state aid numbers and noted regional transportation aid still shows zero on the cherry sheet.
A member questioned spending on an expensive roof for a building whose future is uncertain amid the municipal building debate.
The board agreed to raise the threshold below which the town manager can accept gifts without select board approval.

A member argued that showing cost growth like health insurance on graphs communicates budget pressure better than numbers alone.

decisions.decision: Town manager authorized to finalize which four classrooms will be used in the Shapiro license agreement once the facilities director confirms availability.

Budget task force membership set at one select board member, one school committee member, two finance committee members, and one citizen at-large, with staff attending as non-voting support.
Budget task force to give periodic updates to the select board with a final report due by December 31.

minutes.headline: Select Board again declined to call a special election on the FY26 school override town meeting had approved.
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard extensive public pressure to call a special election on the FY26 Prop 2.5 override that passed narrowly at town meeting, but a majority of members reaffirmed their opposition to putting it on the ballot, citing fiscal concerns and lack of a multi-year plan. The board also set the membership and timeline for a budget task force meant to produce a longer-term fiscal plan, discussed a critical tax investigation report on the 2023 assessment error, approved routine license, appointment, and gift items, and entered executive session on opiate litigation.

what_happened.line: A majority of the Select Board again declined to call a special election on the FY26 override that town meeting narrowly approved.
The board set the membership and year-end deadline for a new budget task force meant to produce a multi-year fiscal plan.
Several residents in public comment challenged the board's authority to withhold the override from a ballot after town meeting passed it.
A tax investigation report on the 2023 lakefront assessment error was discussed but sent back for revisions rather than resolved.
The board authorized the town manager to finalize a summer-program classroom license agreement at TC Pacios.

why_it_matters: Residents who voted for the FY26 Proposition 2.5 override at town meeting will not get a special election ballot this cycle, so the additional funding it would raise stays unresolved for now.
The budget task force, due to report by year end, is meant to shape whether and how a future override or multi-year school funding plan comes back to voters.
The still-unresolved tax investigation into the 2023 assessment error touches how abatements and revenue losses on lakefront properties were handled, which bears on other taxpayers' bills.
